reason: Selected matched-supervision and attack-family results motivate evaluating memory authenticity separately from channel provenance.

candidates.title: Test memory updates against same-origin contamination
candidates.rule: When admitting contradictory user-memory updates, evaluate genuine preference changes, temporary context switches and attacker-like same-origin statements separately instead of relying only on recency or source channel.
candidates.passage: Provenance-only beats Capture on indirect injection
candidates.finding: A provenance-only proxy is better on indirect injection but worse on same-origin contamination. History-aware supervised methods improve the adaptation/poisoning trade-off; most gains are shared with a supervision-matched Transformer. The admission-testing rule is inferred.
candidates.conditions: Compare legitimate revisions and scoped temporary preferences with poisoning under the same memory and response budgets.
candidates.limitations: Synthetic histories and limited human validation constrain prevalence claims. Adaptive-attack superiority is not reliably separated from provenance filtering. The theorem limits rules using particular features under assumptions, not every conceivable fixed heuristic.
candidates.validation_test: Construct independent update episodes with genuine changes, sarcasm, temporary scope and same-origin contamination; report true-update adherence, false admission, poisoning and clarification burden separately.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
